newsitem.title: USA: Aetrium sees Q3, Q4 net below estimates.
newsitem.headline: Aetrium sees Q3, Q4 net below estimates.

text.p: Aetrium Inc said on Monday its revenue and profit for the third and fourth quarters of 1996 are expected to be significantly below current analysts' expectations, as a result of the continued downturn in the semiconductor industry and strategies that management has employed to address it.

Aetrium, which supplies equipment to the semiconductor industry to test integrated circits, said it expects third quarter revenues of about $13 million and earnings per share of between $0.18 and $0.21, down from a mean analyst estimate carried on First Call of $0.38.
Aetrium said it also expects revenue and earnings will be significantly below current analysts' expectations for the fourth quarter ending December 31.
Aetrium reported earnings of $0.72 for the first half of 1996 on revenues of $34.3 million. Aetrium said it plans to report third quarter financial results in mid-October.

Through the first half of the year, Aetrium said requests for price quotes were running 25 percent ahead of 1995 levels. However, they did not lead to signed orders at the rates that it had hoped, the company said.
It appears that a slump in the semiconductor industry has deepened and the company expects it to continue for a longer period of time, Aetrium president Joseph Levesque said.

The company noted that during the current quarter delivery of some orders were pushed by customers further into the year and some other orders were cancelled due to a downturn in the semiconductor industry.
Based on its lower order rate and a backlog of orders for test handlers of less than 90 days, Aetrium said it is not in the best interests of the company to allow the backlog to continue to decline.

Aetrium said it has taken several actions to address the slowdown including trimming its production levels and monitoring costs. In addition, it has voluntarily contacted some customers to reschedule shipping dates into subsequent periods. No orders have been put at risk.
Aetrium said no layoffs are planned. Managers have taken a reduction in base salaries. The company said it intends to continue to fully fund product development efforts.
